hero.1: Good morning! Welcome to the village.
hero.2: Learn Slovene by living in a little village.
hero.3: An Android game with a pixel-art village whose people speak to you, a grammar book that opens as you go, and your own Claude Code session as the tutor behind it, writing new dialogs, stories and exercises as you progress.
hero.8: Early, active development · one daily learner · self-hosted · <abbr title="GNU Affero General Public License 3.0 or later">AGPL</abbr>
hero.9: The village by day: autumn trees round a palisade, the fire in the middle, a few request bubbles over the villagers; the camera flies in to the fire and pans slowly across the village.
hero.10: The village, recorded on the emulator: drawn in code, every pixel of it.
villages.3: Lani has four villages, each in its own language and its own corner of the Alps and beyond: Slovene in Primorska, Italian in Friuli, German in Kärnten and English in the Lake District. Each has its own people, stories, feasts and food. The app's interface speaks Slovene, English, German and Italian, and pairs any two of them: the language you learn, and the one it's explained in.
villages.4: The villagers talk to the learner by name, and their lines agree with the learner's gender, as the language needs: Slovene fant or dekle, Italian ragazzo or ragazza.
villages.12: All of it is real content from the app's culture packs (companion/cultures/), machine-written and marked so until a native speaker has read it. The screenshots are the app on the emulator, visiting sample towns.
village.3: A dozen villagers live their own days. France mows in the dew and harvests his field, Tone forges at the smithy, Babica Micka bakes potica and brings soup to the fire, and every evening Stari Janez tells a legend there. They ask for help in Slovene: a bubble over someone's head is a request, a little exercise in what they need.
village.4: What you do for them builds the village. It starts as a campfire in a clearing and grows with the words you learn, age by age, towards your target level:
village.11: The village keeps time with yours: mornings, rain, the moon, a merchant from Gorizia at the gate, a feast under the linden. Its sounds are synthesized in code too. Have a listen:
village.21: Mojca at the well: the dual!
village.27: The village at night, close to the fire: the windows glow, Stari Janez waits with his story and Babica Micka with her soup, a bubble over each.
village.28: The same village after dark: Stari Janez has a story, Babica Micka brings soup.
scenes.3: Every place of the village opens into a close-up: indoors an isometric diorama, outdoors a view to the hills. You find the words in the picture by tapping the things in it, and you talk to whoever is there today.
scenes.4: The kitchen as an isometric diorama: a stove, a table with bread and a jug, shelves, a red-checked curtain, a vegetable bed outside the wall.
scenes.6: The field as a view to the hills: a hayrack full of hay, a horse and cart on the path, a scarecrow, cabbages, a hare, a church on the hill behind.
scenes.8: In the field, the learner taps the scarecrow, a hare, the hayrack, the cart and the cabbages; each opens its word: strašilo, zajec, kozolec, voz, zelje, and the count of found words goes up.
scenes.9: Find the words in the picture
scenes.10: Tap the scarecrow and it says strašilo, with its gender and plural and a sentence to go with it. Some things show only at dawn, by night, or not in winter; the panel under the picture keeps count of what's here now, what you've seen before and what's still hidden.
scenes.12: A dialog's turns adapt to what you know. While a rule is new, you choose; once you have it, you type the missing word; some turns are answered by tapping the picture, and any turn can be said aloud instead. The dialogs only ask for what the grammar book says you've met.
scenes.18: In the evening Babica Micka brings soup to the fire. Three answers, one right: the others are near misses that teach something (žejen is thirsty, dobro jutro is for the morning).
scenes.19: Good evening, Jan! Are you hungry?
scenes.21: Zala counts with you, then hides. The turn is »Poišči v prizoru«, find it in the scene. The learner taps under the table, and that's the answer:
scenes.24: A cold morning by the fire. Luka is young and a friend, so it's ti: the imperative is sedi, not sedite. The keyboard comes up with the letters č, š and ž ready.
scenes.25: Good morning, Luka! Of course, sit down.
scenes.27: Every line in the app is made of words you can tap. Each opens its card: the dictionary word, what this form is, its meaning, its partner, its forms.
scenes.28: Good evening! Sit down, sit down.
scenes.29: Tap a word on the left.
grammar.1: · Mojca at the well: the dual!
grammar.3: The village scroll, a book once the hamlet is a village, has a page for every rule: 44 for Slovene, from biti to the six cases, aspect and the dual. A page is written in the first time you meet its rule in an exercise, and its stars say how well you know it.
grammar.4: Rules you've only met in the dialogs wait, greyed: »Še ne«, not yet. The dialogs and the word forms only ask what the book has opened, your mistakes show up on the rule's page, and the tutor can write a new page when you need one.
grammar.5: The village scroll's grammar section: rules met so far with their stars (adjectives, adverbs, the genitive after prepositions), and greyed pages only met in the dialogs (the instrumental, the dative).
grammar.6: A grammar page, Tožilnik: pijem kavo, vidim brata (the accusative), with the rule, a table of noun kinds and examples to listen to.
grammar.7: The six cases, on one house
grammar.8: Each case has its school questions. Ask the question, and the answer takes its case. Pick a row.
grammar.19: Slovene has a dual: one form for exactly two. After a number the noun changes, and so does the verb.
words.3: A review question: fill in the right form of miza, the genitive singular, in a sentence from the story of King Matjaž. The learner picks mize; Pravilno! A new page in the grammar book opens: the genitive.
words.4: Words stay with spaced repetition (SM-2): a card comes back just before you'd forget it. A word you remember each time waits longer and longer:
words.7: The cards take many forms: flashcards, listening, dictation, speaking. Once you know a word, its forms come too: its conjugations and cases, as far as the grammar book has opened them, each in a sentence from the village. »Zaklenjene odpre stran v knjigi«: a page of the book opens the locked ones.
words.8: A villager keeps you company in the reviews. In the clip it's Teta Ančka: »Kaj? Kdo ste? Glasneje!« (What? Who are you? Louder!)
car.3: For long drives there's an Android Auto mode: audio drills prepared on the phone ahead of time and played with the steering wheel's buttons. You hear the meaning, say it aloud, then hear how it's said and repeat it.
car.4: Preobrat Transformations: Micka kuha kosilo. Into the past! → Micka je kuhala kosilo.
car.5: Hitri odziv Rapid fire: a number, a time, a date, two seconds to say it.
car.6: Gradnja stavkov Sentence building: a sentence grows a step at a time.
car.7: Uganke Riddles: Stari Janez describes a thing of the village in three or four clues.
car.8: The phone's player while a drive plays: only the meaning shows, snow, oven, to think, a pan, then a dialog from the kitchen; the learner says the Slovene aloud before hearing it.
car.9: The phone's player during a drive: it shows only the meaning (snow, oven, to think), you say the Slovene first. Sped up 2.5×.
car.10: While driving, don't look at the screen.
car.15: The car's sheet in the app, 🚗 Za pot · For the road: everything for the road is on the phone, 14 minutes to listen to, and the sessions: for the road, easy listening, shadowing, reviews, new words, dialogs, stories, transformations.
visits.3: From the Friends screen, the learner visits Borgo di Prova, an Italian test town: the banner says In visita · Visiting, the labels turn Italian, Nonna Rosa greets with Vieni, vieni. Siediti., and the gift panel offers Tolminc cheese, potica and a message in the town's language.
visits.4: Every learner's village is a town of its own, and towns can link up: two learners, each with their own tutor, can visit each other's village. Towns are linked only by invitation, with a one-time QR code or code that works for 30 minutes. There's no directory.
visits.5: A visit happens in the host village's language. Visit an Italian town and its labels read In visita · Visiting, its people greet you in Italian, and everything you learn there goes to your Italian. Both learners practise the language of the village they're in.
visits.6: Things to do on a visit
visits.7: Requests: help the town's people with a run of their words, and they thank you with something from their chest.
visits.8: A gift: something from your chest and a short message, written in the town's language.
visits.9: The market: pick what you'd like, offer something of yours, and haggle; your tutor plays the seller.
visits.10: A question for the host: ask in their language; they answer in it. Each tutor checks its own learner's sentence first, if they like.
visits.11: Talk: the town's people, played by your own tutor, in the town's language.
visits.12: The Friends screen: your town, Invite and Accept buttons, and a linked town, Borgo di Prova (Marta), at the friendship level Znanstvo · Acquaintance, with a Visit button.
visits.13: Friends: linked towns and how close they are.
visits.14: Requests in the visited town: Nonna Rosa's kitchen (she makes frico but forgot some words) and Franco's list, each with a Help button.
visits.16: The market of the visited town: it offers honey, Montasio cheese and frico; the visitor offers Tolminc cheese, potica and linden tea.
visits.18: Asking the host a question: Chiedi a Marta · Ask Marta, with the question Come si chiama il tuo cane? and the buttons Check and Send.
visits.19: A question for the host: Come si chiama il tuo cane?
visits.20: A friendship both towns agree on
visits.21: Visits, help, gifts, trades and answered questions count for the towns' friendship, which grows through five levels. Each brings something: better rates at the market, help when wolves or a storm come, a shared feast, people moving between the towns. Both towns compute the level from the same counts, and an act counts once both have it, so a friendship that one learner keeps up alone stops at the middle.
visits.28: A town shows its linked towns only its public state: its buildings, its people, its age and today's weather. Never the learner's chat, mistakes, words or progress. Every request between towns is signed with the town's own key; an unlinked town gets nothing.
visits.30: A child's village is linked by a parent, on the machine, never from the child's phone. It takes no question with a link or an address in it, its tutor keeps every exchange age-appropriate, and the parent sees every question and answer.
stories.3: Every evening Stari Janez sits by the fire and tells a legend in chapters, at your level, and asks you along the way: Martin Krpan, Zlatorog, Kralj Matjaž, Peter Klepec. In the other villages it's Nonno Bepi, Opa Sepp and Old Wilf.
stories.4: The campfire scene at night as an isometric diorama: a pot over the fire, a woodpile, Stari Janez on a log, a bubble with a book over him.
stories.6: Each story is written down in your notebook, »Moj zvezek zgodb«, in a hand-drawn style with pencil sketches taped in: every story you've heard, to read again, listen to, and be quizzed on.
stories.7: Stari Janez's evening story: Dober večer, Jan. Nocoj ti povem zgodbo o Petru Klepcu. Poznaš Petra? The learner picks Ne, ne poznam ga. Kdo je to? and the story begins.
stories.8: The story notebook's first page in handwriting on lined paper: Zapisano ob ognju, written down by the fire, and its contents: Zlatorog, Kralj Matjaž, Martin Krpan, with dates.
stories.9: A notebook page of Zlatorog: lines of the story in blue ink, and a pencil sketch taped in of the white fairies and the golden-horned chamois under the mountains.
stories.10: Zlatorog, the white chamois with golden horns.
tutor.1: · Aunt Ančka listens to the radio
tutor.3: Behind the app runs a Claude Code session on your machine: your tutor. The app's chat goes straight to it. It knows what you got wrong yesterday, answers about any exercise, and builds the content as you progress:
tutor.4: new dialogs, scenes and villagers' lines, at your level
tutor.6: word packs and practice modules for your weak spots
tutor.7: fixes for anything you report as wrong, with what it cost you given back
tutor.8: It publishes them to the app through the bridge's MCP tools, and the phone shows them at once. In the chat you can bookmark an answer, reply to a message from last week, or look things up in the archive.
tutor.9: The tutor's skills grew from m98/fluent, the AI language learning kit for Claude Code. It also works on its own, in the terminal.
tutor.10: An example conversation with the tutor
tutor.14: Sedite is the vi form: Babica is talking to several of you, or politely to one. To one friend it's sedi, as you told Luka this morning.
tutor.15: Both are sesti, to sit down. Sitting there already is sedeti: Babica sedi pri ognju.
tutor.18: ✨ New in the village: a short drill on ti and vi for tomorrow.
how.4: The Android app talks to the bridge over HTTP and server-sent events, through your tailnet. The bridge, a Bun program on your machine, keeps your data as JSON files there and talks to your Claude Code session, the tutor, over an MCP channel. The tutor publishes dialogs, stories, grammar pages and modules back through the bridge to the app.
how.17: How Lani fits together: the app talks to the bridge over HTTP and SSE through your tailnet; on your machine the bridge keeps your data and talks to the Claude Code tutor over MCP.
how.26: The app, in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose. The village, the scenes and the people are drawn in code.
how.27: Serves the app, keeps your data (progress, mistakes, reviews, the village) as JSON on your machine, in a git repository of its own, and lets the tutor publish content.
how.28: The villages and their people, the scenes and stories, the grammar pages: content anyone can read and correct.
how.29: The tutor's skills and hooks. LEARNING_SYSTEM.md is its method: active recall, SM-2, immediate feedback.
run.3: Lani runs self-hosted today: the bridge and the tutor on a machine of yours that stays on (Linux or macOS), the app on your Android phone. There is no hosted version and no store release. You need Claude Code with a Claude plan or API key, Bun and an Android phone.
run.4: Get Lani and run the setup wizard: the learner, their data, voices, the network, pairing
run.6: Start your tutor (tmux; detach with Ctrl-b d)
run.8: Get the app onto your phone: the latest release from GitHub, sent over Tailscale (or adb install over USB)
run.10: Pair the phone: scan the QR code in the app
run.12: The data stays on your machine, in a git repository of its own, committed after each session. The guide, and every step by hand: docs/setup.md; what leaves your machine: docs/privacy.md; the rest (Tailscale, voices, speech recognition, the bridge as a service, backups): companion/README.md.
open.3: Lani is free software under the GNU Affero General Public License 3.0 or later. It began as a fork of m98/fluent by Mohammad Kermani and the Fluent contributors (MIT); the parts from it stay available under MIT as well.
open.4: Corrections to the Slovene are especially welcome: much of the content is machine-written and marked so until a native speaker has read it. The same goes for this site's Slovene, German and Italian. See CONTRIBUTING.md.

js.meta.title: Lani · Learn Slovene in a little village
js.meta.description: Lani is an Android game for learning Slovene: a pixel-art village whose people speak to you, a grammar book that opens as you go, and your own Claude Code session as the tutor behind it. Villages in four languages that visit each other. Free software (AGPL).
js.dialog.soup: Babica Micka brings soup to the fire in the evening. She asks: Dober večer, Jan! Si lačen? The learner picks Dober večer! Ja, zelo sem lačen. She answers Potem sedi k ognju, and offers the soup.
js.dialog.hide: Zala plays hide-and-seek in the living room. The learner counts to ten, Zala hides, and the turn asks to find her in the scene: the learner taps under the table. Aha, pod mizo si! Joj! Kako si me našel tako hitro?
js.dialog.typed: Luka warms his hands by the fire in the morning. The turn asks to type the missing word: Dobro jutro, Luka! Seveda, blank. The keyboard comes up, the panel rises over the picture, the learner types sedi and checks. Luka answers Hvala. Ogenj lepo gori.

js.wc.dober.title: masculine · feminine · neuter
js.wc.dober.note: An adjective takes its noun's gender: dober dan, dobra kava, dobro jutro.
js.wc.vecer.title: singular
js.wc.vecer.note: Dobro jutro in the morning, dober dan by day, dober večer in the evening, lahko noč at bedtime.
js.wc.sedite.partner.gram: second-person plural present; second-person plural imperative
js.wc.sedite.partner.note: sesti: a movement, once · sedeti: a state that lasts
js.wc.sedite.title: present
js.wc.sedite.note: Sedite is for several people, or one you say vi to. To one friend: sedi!
js.case.0.why: kdo? kaj? The base form, the one in the dictionary.
js.case.1.en: Near the house there's a linden.
js.case.1.why: blizu takes the genitive, like iz, od and do.
js.case.2.why: k takes the dative: towards someone or something.
js.case.3.why: The object of the verb: the accusative.
js.case.4.en: There's a garden by the house.
js.case.4.why: pri takes the locative: where, at whose place.
js.case.5.en: There's a bench in front of the house.
js.case.5.why: s, pred, za, pod and nad take the instrumental: s hišo, with the house.

js.quiz.0.meta:
sesti — to sit down
1st person singular, present
js.quiz.0.en: I sit down on the bench.
js.quiz.0.ok: Na klop answers kam? (where to?) with the accusative: a movement, so sesti.
js.quiz.0.no.sedim: Sedim is sedeti, to be sitting, and goes with kje? (where?): Jaz sedim na klopi. Na klop is where to: sesti, sedem.
js.quiz.0.no.sedeš: Sedeš is ti: you sit down. For jaz: sedem.
js.quiz.0.no.sede: Sede is on or ona: he or she sits down. For jaz: sedem.
js.quiz.1.meta:
sedeti — to be sitting
3rd person singular, present
js.quiz.1.en: Grandma is sitting by the fire.
js.quiz.1.ok: Pri ognju (pri with the locative) says where she is: a state, sedeti.
js.quiz.1.no.sede: Sede is sesti, sitting down: Babica sede k ognju, she goes and sits down. Pri ognju is where she is: sedi.
js.quiz.1.no.sedijo: Sedijo is oni, three or more of them. For babica: sedi.
js.quiz.1.no.sedim: Sedim is jaz: I am sitting. For babica: sedi.

js.quiz.2.no.miza: Miza is the base form (kdo? kaj?). Okoli takes the genitive: mize.
js.quiz.2.no.mizo: Mizo is the accusative or the instrumental (vidim mizo, za mizo). Okoli takes the genitive: mize.

hiša — house

js.v.primorska.about: A village on the Trnovo plateau above Nova Gorica: the hills of Brda, Gorizia across the border, the burja, rebula and potica. The first village, with the most content.
js.v.friuli.about: A village in the Collio hills near Gorizia, facing Brda across the border: the Isonzo, Monte Sabotino, the grape harvest, frico, gubana and ribolla gialla.
js.v.kaernten.about: A village in the lower Gailtal below the Dobratsch, near Villach, where Austria, Slovenia and Italy meet: the lakes, the Karawanken, the Kirchtag, Kasnudeln and Reindling.
js.v.lakeland.about: A dale village among the fells of the Lake District, between Keswick and Grasmere: tarns and becks, drystone walls, Herdwick sheep, tatie pot and sticky toffee pudding.
